findings.issue_text: [High/bug] In src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py (~line 148), gen_request_data compares nodestore event timestamps (ISO-8601 string / epoch seconds in event node data) against replay segment event timestamps (epoch milliseconds) with '<', raising TypeError and 500ing every summarize request for replays with errors when the value is a string, or silently breaking chronological interleaving (all error messages sort before all breadcrumbs) due to the 1000x seconds-vs-milliseconds unit gap; the ErrorEvent.timestamp: float annotation doesn't match what nodestore actually returns.

[Medium/bug] In src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py (~line 118), fetch_error_details uses zip(error_ids, events.values()), assuming nodestore.backend.get_multi returns values in the same order and completeness as error_ids; get_multi returns a mapping keyed by node id that can omit missing rows and order cache hits before backend fetches, so error titles/messages/timestamps can be attributed to the wrong event_id — should key by node id (events.get(node_id) while zipping error_ids with node_ids) instead.

[Medium/data] In src/sentry/preprod/api/endpoints/organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py (~line 81), analytics.record('preprod_artifact.api.assemble', ...) fires before the feature-gate check and before any payload validation, so requests rejected by the feature flag or that fail validation/assembly are still counted as successful 'assemble' events, skewing usage metrics; should record after the gate and successful assembly.

[Low/api] In src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py (~line 108), the first invalid report returns 422 and discards all other valid reports in the same POST; per the Reporting API the browser retries the entire batch, so one persistently malformed report permanently blocks ingestion of the valid ones — should skip invalid reports and process the rest (none of the age/timestamp/attempts fields are even used downstream).

[Low/bug] In src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py (~line 41), attempts = serializers.IntegerField(min_value=1) may reject valid reports: the Reporting API defines attempts as the number of failed delivery attempts, which is 0 on first delivery, and the previous code accepted 0; should verify against real browser payloads before enforcing this bound.

[Low/api] The project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py endpoint (~line 67) now calls get_filter_params(request, project), which requires statsPeriod or start/end, whereas previously it required no query params; existing callers that don't send a date range will now fail — should pass optional=True or default the range.

[Low/performance] In src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py (~line 70), the Snuba query_replay_instance + process_raw_response queries run even when enable_error_context=false, and the fetched error_ids are then discarded; should move them under the flag check.

[Low/performance] In src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py (~line 587), get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() (nodestore/eventstore fetch) once per issue inside the merged-PR comment loop, adding up to 5 extra event fetches per posted comment; should batch these or confirm the latency is acceptable in the comment-posting path.

[Low/data] Gutting already-merged migrations 0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py and 0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised.py to no-ops is only safe if no environment (including staging/getsentry) applied or partially applied them; any environment where 0917/0920 crashed mid-run now depends entirely on 0921 being idempotent to converge.

[Low/test_gap] The new error-context merging logic in src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py (fetch_error_details alignment, gen_request_data timestamp interleaving) ships with no accompanying unit tests in the diff; the type/ordering bugs would have been caught by straightforward tests over fixture segment/error data.

goldens.comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.

Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] In src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py (~line 148), gen_request_data compares nodestore event timestamps (ISO-8601 string / epoch seconds in event node data) against replay segment event timestamps (epoch milliseconds) with '<', raising TypeError and 500ing every summarize request for replays with errors when the value is a string, or silently breaking chronological interleaving (all error messages sort before all breadcrumbs) due to the 1000x seconds-vs-milliseconds unit gap; the ErrorEvent.timestamp: float annotation doesn't match what nodestore actually returns.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ErrorEvent.timestamp` is populated as `data.get("timestamp", 0.0)` in `fetch_error_details`, and replay segment events are compared against `event.get("timestamp", 0)` in `gen_request_data`. Nothing in the diff indicates nodestore returns an ISO-8601 string timestamp, nor that replay segment timestamps are in milliseconds; in fact, the added tests construct both breadcrumb and error timestamps as plain floats in epoch *seconds* (e.g., 1.5, 2.0, 3.0 and `now.timestamp()`), and validate correct chronological interleaving. Any seconds-vs-milliseconds or string-vs-float TypeError claim depends on external knowledge not evidenced by this PR diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] In src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py (~line 108), the first invalid report returns 422 and discards all other valid reports in the same POST; per the Reporting API the browser retries the entire batch, so one persistently malformed report permanently blocks ingestion of the valid ones — should skip invalid reports and process the rest (none of the age/timestamp/attempts fields are even used downstream).

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint.post`, reports are validated in a loop and the handler returns immediately on the first invalid report (`if not serializer.is_valid(): ... return Response(..., 422)`). This means a batch containing any malformed report will cause all other (potentially valid) reports in the same POST to be dropped/not processed (no `metrics.incr` for them). That all-or-nothing behavior is directly shown by the diff and can lead to valid reports being blocked by a persistently invalid one in the batch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] In src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py (~line 41), attempts = serializers.IntegerField(min_value=1) may reject valid reports: the Reporting API defines attempts as the number of failed delivery attempts, which is 0 on first delivery, and the previous code accepted 0; should verify against real browser payloads before enforcing this bound.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds strict validation in `BrowserReportSerializer` with `attempts = serializers.IntegerField(min_value=1)`, whereas the prior implementation (`BrowserReport` dataclass) performed no bounds checking and would have accepted `0`. This is a behavior change that could reject some previously-accepted payloads. However, the diff itself does not establish the Reporting API’s required semantics for `attempts` (whether `0` is valid on first delivery), so it can’t be conclusively verified as a definite bug from the PR alone—only as a potentially-too-strict validation choice introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] The project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py endpoint (~line 67) now calls get_filter_params(request, project), which requires statsPeriod or start/end, whereas previously it required no query params; existing callers that don't send a date range will now fail — should pass optional=True or default the range.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get now calling `self.get_filter_params(request, project)` and using `filter_params["start"]`/`["end"]` for `query_replay_instance`, but nothing in the diff establishes that `get_filter_params` *requires* statsPeriod/start/end or would fail without them. In fact, the updated tests still call `self.client.get(self.url)` with no date-range query params and assert 200 responses, which contradicts the claim that callers without a date range will now fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] In src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py (~line 70), the Snuba query_replay_instance + process_raw_response queries run even when enable_error_context=false, and the fetched error_ids are then discarded; should move them under the flag check.

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, the code always computes `filter_params`, then runs `query_replay_instance(...)` and `process_raw_response(...)` to derive `error_ids` before checking `enable_error_context` (via `disable_error_fetching`). When `enable_error_context=false`, it sets `error_events = []` and discards `error_ids`, so the Snuba query/processing work is unnecessary in that path. This is a diff-grounded performance concern rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] In src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py (~line 587), get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() (nodestore/eventstore fetch) once per issue inside the merged-PR comment loop, adding up to 5 extra event fetches per posted comment; should batch these or confirm the latency is acceptable in the comment-posting path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `CommitContextIntegration.get_environment_info()` which calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` (commit_context.py) and is invoked inside the per-issue loop when building merged-PR comments in both GitHub and GitLab integrations (`get_comment_body` now calls `self.get_environment_info(issue)` for each issue). This adds an extra per-issue lookup on the comment-posting path (up to the number of issues included), which is a concrete performance/latency concern even if it may be acceptable; batching/caching or confirming latency would be reasonable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] Gutting already-merged migrations 0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py and 0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised.py to no-ops is only safe if no environment (including staging/getsentry) applied or partially applied them; any environment where 0917/0920 crashed mid-run now depends entirely on 0921 being idempotent to converge.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes both data migrations 0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py and 0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised.py from performing DB transforms to unconditional no-ops (`return`) with a comment saying they "were never run" and deferring to 0921. While this isn’t a directly provable defect from the diff alone (we can’t verify historical execution state of these migrations in all environments), the finding raises a concrete, diff-grounded operational concern: if any environment had applied/partially applied 0917/0920, converting them to no-ops would prevent re-running their intended behavior and places full convergence burden on 0921’s idempotency. That’s a legitimate review risk tied to this change, not a hallucination.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] The new error-context merging logic in src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py (fetch_error_details alignment, gen_request_data timestamp interleaving) ships with no accompanying unit tests in the diff; the type/ordering bugs would have been caught by straightforward tests over fixture segment/error data.

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* add/extend unit tests covering the new error-context merging logic in `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`: `tests/sentry/replays/test_project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py` adds `test_get_with_error`, `test_get_with_error_context_disabled`, and updates `test_get_request_data` to validate timestamp-based interleaving of breadcrumb logs with `ErrorEvent` entries. Therefore the claim that the logic ships with no accompanying unit tests is contradicted by the diff.
